subject.title: Feature request: cron job auto-retry on failure (--retry-count, --retry-delay)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job cron retry controls on top of the shipped global `cron.retry` policy, and should maintainers adopt/rework the linked fork PR or require a fresh design?
rationale: This changes public CLI flags, Gateway schema, persisted cron job shape, retry defaults, and side-effecting scheduler semantics, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Approve additive per-job overrides
options.body: Define per-job retry fields as additive overrides that preserve current global behavior for existing jobs and review or rework the linked PR against that contract.

options.title: Keep only global retry
options.body: Close or narrow this request if maintainers decide the shipped global `cron.retry` policy is the supported recovery model.

options.title: Fold into reason-aware guardrails
options.body: Defer per-job retry controls until the broader cron guardrail policy in the related reason-aware issue is settled.

recommendation.title: Approve additive per-job overrides
recommendation.body: Define per-job retry fields as additive overrides that preserve current global behavior for existing jobs and review or rework the linked PR against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the merged recurring retry implementation and has the strongest recent history on the scheduler behavior this decision extends.
